You're just negotiating with comfort.

A NOTE FROM TIM...

I applaud everyone getting out of their comfort zone to create change — monthly, weekly, daily. But really, it comes down to moment by moment. Right now I'm negotiating one: stay at my computer, or get out in the heat for the run my HYROX training needs. The AC just clicked on. The cool air makes the wrong choice feel a lot more tempting.

Three things are tipping me toward the run anyway:

  1. A time-sensitive goal. Seven weeks from today, we're in DC for race #4 (race #3, a relay, is seven weeks out this past Friday). And I'm not doing these alone — not wanting to let the team down adds real fuel.
  2. A decision made in advance. I set the time for this run last night, before I ever felt the heat or heard the AC.
  3. Accountability. Someone else is enrolled in this goal with me.

None of these erase the discomfort — the heat's still the heat. What they do is stack the odds in favor of the version of me that shows up.

That's the whole philosophy behind LNGVTY Hub: 1º changes. Small, repeatable decisions that remove friction from doing the right thing again tomorrow. One degree doesn't feel like much in the moment. Compounded over 7 weeks, 7 months, 7 years — it's the difference between the body that negotiates and the body that's already out the door.

So this week, negotiate smarter. Set the time. Tell someone. Give yourself a deadline that matters more than the comfort in front of you.

See you at The Hub.
- Tim

lemon cookies

These keto lemon cookies are a low carb and sugar free take on classic lemon crinkle cookies! Simple ingredients and ready in just 15 minutes!

—

—
—

Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large mixing bowl, combine almond flour, salt, granulated sweetener, and lemon zest. Mix well.
In another bowl, beat the egg whites until soft peaks form. Add lemon extract and yellow food coloring (if using). Gently fold this mixture into the dry ingredients until well combined.
Place the sugar-free powdered sugar in a separate bowl. Using a 1 tablespoon cookie scoop, scoop out heaping tablespoons of dough and roll them in the powdered sugar until fully coated. Place them on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake the cookies for about 15 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden and the tops begin to crackle.
Remove from the oven and let the cookies cool completely on a wire rack. If some of the powdered sugar has melted into the cookies while baking, you can sprinkle more powdered sugar on top once they are cooled.
